newsitem.title: MEXICO: Accel sees sales rebounding in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Accel sees sales rebounding in 1997.

text.p: The planning director of Mexican holding company Accel on Tuesday forecast a rebound in growth in 1997 after a difficult time for its clothing division this year.

"There's been an important slowdown because of the situation of clothing consumption (in the United States). The market is at a standstill," Arturo Lardizabal told Reuters, referring to sales of Accel's Florida-based Tropical Sportswear International unit.
But he forecast "important growth" for Tropical next year, though not quite as agressive as the average 20 percent sales growth he said it had recorded in past years.
He also said the firm's main unit, contract manufacturer Elamex, was expected to have sales growth near to an estimated 20-25 percent in coming years.
Analysts say this year its profits may be chequered by a strengthening peso that hits its dollar-paying clients.
Accel's stock has soared some 20 percent in the Mexican market this month to a price of 13.16 from 11 pesos, and has led gainers in the last two days.
On Tuesday, volume was a healthy 129,000 shares, with BBV Probursa, that recently reiterated a buy recommendation on the stock, handling the bulk of the transactions.
"The company is very cheap. Probably the market is only just taking this into account," said BBV Probursa analyst Evelia Barragan.
